status: landed as correct simplifications with no measurable speedup. Both changes are provably result-neutral and provably do strictly less work, but interleaved A/B shows them inside the noise floor on all four fixture/intent cells. No latency claim is made.

item_2_per_root_reachability_walk.change: validate_machine_plan_row_expression_reachability now calls the arena's walk_postorder_many once with every root instead of looping walk_postorder per root
item_2_per_root_reachability_walk.why_it_was_duplicate_work: each single-root call allocated its own visited set and re-walked every shared child, so a child reachable from N roots was walked, ordered and inserted N times
item_2_per_root_reachability_walk.why_it_did_not_pay: walk_postorder_many was already implemented and already used internally at boon_plan/src/lib.rs:9119; the reachability roots overlap little in practice, so the duplicated walking was a small fraction of a phase that is not itself dominant
item_2_per_root_reachability_walk.mechanical_note: walk_postorder_many was private and is now public; no behavioural change to the walk itself

item_4_arena_intern_double_hash.change: intern now hands its already-computed canonical_sha256 to a new private push_with_key, instead of calling push which recomputed the identical hash and re-ran validate_new_node
item_4_arena_intern_double_hash.why_it_was_duplicate_work: a miss cost two canonical CBOR+SHA-256 passes over the same node plus a second validate_new_node walk
item_4_arena_intern_double_hash.why_it_did_not_pay: the affected phase is the plan backend's derived_values/document lowering, which is not where either fixture's time is concentrated (kernel compile and solve dominate typecheck; the verified-only phases are a minority of total)
item_4_arena_intern_double_hash.rejected_alternative: comparing nodes before hashing was implemented first and immediately reverted: it converts a hash-index lookup into a linear scan over every node, which is far worse. Threading the key through is strictly better and digest-identical.

correctness_gate.per_observation_identity: one distinct (diagnostics_fingerprint, plan_sha256) per lane in all four cells, and identical across lanes
correctness_gate.tests: boon_plan lib 59 passed; boon_compiler_kernel lib 198 passed

measurement.protocol: interleaved A/B/A, one process per observation, producers alternating by observation index, 3 setup + 30 scored per fixture and intent, diagnostics and verified
measurement.host_caveat: a Firefox content process held ~205% CPU throughout, so absolute variance is high. Interleaving keeps the comparison unbiased, and min is reported because background load can inflate a sample but cannot push the minimum below the uncontended cost.
measurement.verdict: neutral. min, the most contamination-robust statistic here, is within +/-1.3% in every cell with no consistent sign. The single -9.21% p95 is a contention artifact and is not treated as a result.
measurement.note_on_the_estimate: the plan predicted 300-450 ms for M1 as a whole. That figure was never attributed to specific items, and items 2 and 4 demonstrably do not deliver it. The unattributed share sits in items 5 and 6, which change hash computation and are still unbuilt.

items.decision: KEEP, as a correct simplification, not as a speedup
decision_reasoning: Both changes remove work that is provably redundant, verified by the byte-identical digests.
Neither is a risk: no semantic change, no schema change, no budget change, and both test suites are green.
The alternative is reverting correct, tested simplifications on the grounds that their benefit is unmeasurable at this scale, which would be churn.
No latency claim is attached to this commit, and none should be quoted from it.
consequences_for_the_plan: M1 items 2 and 4 are DONE with no measured payoff. Items 1 and 3 are parked with recorded reasons (different phases with an authoritative gate; a borrow-checker workaround whose partial fix restructures a borrow).
M1 items 5 and 6 remain the only M1 items with a plausible material payoff, and both change hash computation, so they require the controlled oracle migration rather than a plan-hash check.
The plan's 300-450 ms estimate for M1 should be treated as unattributed until items 5 and 6 are individually measured.

M3 is now the highest-value open item: the invocation-frame probe found 5,487 singleton frames on TodoMVC (94.8%) and 671 on NovyWave (95.4%), backed by non-zero production counters. The correct next step is the solve-side probe, not an implementation.
caveats: The host was contended throughout, so this measurement bounds the effect as 'no larger than about 1%', not as 'exactly zero'. A quiet-window re-run could tighten the bound but cannot turn four same-signed-neutral cells into a win.
No budget, schema or gate was touched. The stale machine_plan_sha256 finding in compiler-m0-attribution-2026-09-27.json still stands and is still the owner's to decide.
